places.name: Hudson River Greenway
places.blurb: The crown-jewel riverside run of Manhattan's West Side.
places.see: Open Hudson sweep with sailboats, the Palisades cliffs across the water, and uninterrupted sunset light.
places.do: Detour onto Pier 45 or Pier 25 to stand out over the river.
places.tip: Goes for miles flat and car-free; ideal at golden hour.

places.name: Hudson River Park Esplanade
places.blurb: Manicured waterfront promenade threading the Hudson River piers.
places.see: Lawns, flower beds and rebuilt piers framing the river and New Jersey skyline.
places.do: Wander out onto Little Island, the floating park at Pier 55.
places.tip: Busy with strollers and cyclists midday; run early.

places.name: John Finley Walk
places.blurb: Carl Schurz Park's cantilevered promenade over the East River.
places.see: Roosevelt Island, the Triborough and Hell Gate bridges, and Gracie Mansion behind you.
places.do: Loop down into Carl Schurz Park's shaded paths.
places.tip: Quiet Upper East Side stretch, lovely at sunrise.

places.name: East River Greenway
places.blurb: Lower Manhattan's waterfront path beneath the Brooklyn Bridge.
places.see: The three East River bridges strung overhead and Brooklyn's skyline across the water.
places.do: Stop under the Brooklyn Bridge for the classic upward view.
places.tip: Connects Battery to the bridges; great one-way commute run.

places.name: Battery Park City Greenway
places.blurb: Polished harbor esplanade along Battery Park City.
places.see: Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island out in the harbor across calm water.
places.do: Pause at the Irish Hunger Memorial or the marina at North Cove.
places.tip: Best Statue of Liberty views are near the southern end.

places.name: Roosevelt Island Greenway
places.blurb: A car-light loop around the slender island in the East River.
places.see: Midtown's skyline on one side, Queens on the other, with water on both flanks.
places.do: Ride the aerial tram over the river to start or finish.
places.tip: Head south to Four Freedoms Park's open granite point.

places.name: Riverside Walk
places.blurb: Riverside Park's tree-lined Hudson-side path on the Upper West Side.
places.see: Leafy canopy, the river through the trees, and the 79th Street Boat Basin.
places.do: Stop at the Boat Basin to watch houseboats bob.
places.tip: Shaded and cool in summer; quietest above 90th.

places.name: East Midtown Greenway
places.blurb: A newly built cantilevered link in the East Side waterfront.
places.see: The river right beneath the deck and the Queensboro Bridge soaring ahead.
places.do: Connect north toward John Finley Walk for a longer run.
places.tip: Short but fills a former gap in the East River path.

places.name: East River Esplanade
places.blurb: Open East Side waterfront below the UN and Kips Bay.
places.see: Wide water, passing barges, and Long Island City's towers opposite.
places.do: Detour up to Stuyvesant Cove's pocket gardens.
places.tip: Exposed and windy; bring a layer on cool days.

places.name: Tech Walk
places.blurb: Landscaped campus path through Cornell Tech on Roosevelt Island.
places.see: Modern glass buildings, green roofs, and river framing the skyline.
places.tip: Pairs with the Roosevelt Island loop for a full circuit.

places.name: Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge Path
places.blurb: The bike-and-run crossing between Midtown and Queens.
places.see: Steel lattice overhead, Roosevelt Island below, and a Manhattan skyline reveal.
places.do: Cross into Long Island City for the Gantry Plaza skyline views.
places.tip: A real climb to mid-span; shared with fast cyclists.

places.name: Manhattan Bridge Pedestrian Path
places.blurb: The quieter East River bridge crossing into DUMBO.
places.see: The Brooklyn Bridge perfectly framed, the harbor, and the Lower Manhattan skyline behind.
places.do: Finish in DUMBO under the bridge for the famous Washington Street view.
places.tip: Far less crowded than the Brooklyn Bridge alongside it.

places.name: Riverside Park South Esplanade
places.blurb: Riverfront extension below the Upper West Side's western edge.
places.see: Old railway pier pilings rising from the water and the river opening northward.
places.do: Continue north onto the main Riverside Walk.
places.tip: Connects the Greenway to Riverside Park seamlessly.

places.name: Central Park East Drive
places.blurb: The eastern half of Central Park's iconic loop drive.
places.see: Rolling lawns, the Reservoir, and Fifth Avenue's mansions through the trees.
places.do: Circle the Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir for the skyline-on-water view.
places.tip: Car-free; the full loop is about 6 miles.

places.name: Manhattan Bridge Bike Path
places.blurb: The Brooklyn-side bike lane of the Manhattan Bridge crossing.
places.see: Subway trains rumbling past and the Lower Manhattan skyline ahead.
places.do: Drop into DUMBO at the Brooklyn end.
places.tip: Pair with the pedestrian path for a round trip.

places.name: Central Park
places.blurb: The 843-acre green heart of Manhattan and the city's premier run.
places.see: The Bethesda Terrace, the Lake, Sheep Meadow, and skyline towers rising over the treetops.
places.do: Run the Reservoir loop or climb to Belvedere Castle.
places.tip: Endless car-free routes; quietest at dawn in the North Woods.

places.name: Battery Park
places.blurb: Manhattan's southern tip park looking out over the harbor.
places.see: The Statue of Liberty, passing ferries, and the open expanse of New York Harbor.
places.do: Watch the Staten Island Ferry slide in and out of Whitehall.
places.tip: The harbor views are best in clear morning light.

places.name: Bryant Park
places.blurb: Midtown's elegant lawn behind the New York Public Library.
places.see: The great lawn ringed by London plane trees and skyscrapers on every side.
places.do: Step into the grand Rose Reading Room of the library next door.
places.tip: Winter brings an ice rink; spring brings the lawn back.

places.name: Madison Square Park
places.blurb: Leafy green square beneath the Flatiron Building.
places.see: The wedge of the Flatiron Building, rotating art installations, and shaded lawns.
places.do: Grab the line at the original Shake Shack in the park.
places.tip: Lovely lunchtime stop; the Flatiron view is best from the south.

places.name: Washington Square Park
places.blurb: Greenwich Village's lively heart under its marble arch.
places.see: The Washington Square Arch, the central fountain, and a swirl of street performers.
places.do: Pause for a chess game or piano busker by the fountain.
places.tip: Most alive in late afternoon; a great run-start hub.

places.name: Tompkins Square Park
places.blurb: The East Village's gritty, beloved green commons.
places.see: Towering elms, dog runs, and a constant cast of neighborhood characters.
places.do: Loop the leafy interior paths or catch a free concert.
places.tip: Shady and cool; a good warm-up loop.

places.name: Zuccotti Park
places.blurb: The granite plaza in the heart of the Financial District.
places.see: Skyscraper canyons, the glowing red 'Joie de Vivre' sculpture, and Wall Street crowds.
places.do: Walk a block to the 9/11 Memorial pools.
places.tip: Best as a pass-through on a downtown loop.

places.name: Liberty Park
places.blurb: Elevated green terrace above the World Trade Center site.
places.see: A raised overlook onto the 9/11 Memorial pools and the soaring Oculus.
places.do: Step inside the Oculus transit hall's white ribs.
places.tip: The elevated view of the Memorial is the draw.

places.name: Bowling Green
places.blurb: The city's oldest public park, a small oval at Broadway's foot.
places.see: The Charging Bull statue and the grand old Custom House facade.
places.do: Snap the Charging Bull, then run down Broadway's Canyon of Heroes.
places.tip: Tiny but historic; quick downtown landmark stop.

places.name: Washington Market Park
places.blurb: A green pocket in Tribeca with a Victorian gazebo.
places.see: A lush lawn, flower beds, and a white bandstand amid Tribeca's cast-iron blocks.
places.tip: Calm family-friendly stop on a Tribeca loop.

places.name: One World Observatory
places.blurb: The top-floor observatory of the Western Hemisphere's tallest building.
places.see: A 360-degree panorama from the harbor to Midtown, 100 floors up.
places.do: Time entry for sunset over the harbor.
places.tip: Ticketed; the base sits beside the 9/11 Memorial.

places.name: Top of the Rock
places.blurb: Rockefeller Center's observation deck with the classic skyline shot.
places.see: The Empire State Building dead ahead and Central Park stretching north.
places.do: Go up at dusk to catch the city lights flick on.
places.tip: Best framing of the Empire State Building of any deck.

places.name: Edge
places.blurb: The Western Hemisphere's highest outdoor sky deck at Hudson Yards.
places.see: A glass-floor edge jutting into open air with the Hudson and Midtown below.
places.do: Stand on the glass floor and look straight down 100 stories.
places.tip: Ticketed; pairs with a Hudson Yards / High Line run.

places.name: Summit One Vanderbilt
places.blurb: A mirrored, immersive observation experience beside Grand Central.
places.see: Infinite mirror rooms reflecting the Chrysler Building and Midtown skyline.
places.do: Ride the glass Ascent elevators on the building's exterior.
places.tip: Ticketed; right atop Grand Central Terminal.

places.name: Tudor City Bridge
places.blurb: A small pedestrian bridge with a framed view down 42nd Street.
places.see: The Chrysler Building aligned perfectly down the 42nd Street corridor.
places.do: Set up the famous 42nd-Street-axis photo at sunset.
places.tip: A photographer's secret; arrive near 'Manhattanhenge' dates.

places.name: Staple Street Skybridge
places.blurb: A photogenic copper skybridge over a Tribeca alley.
places.see: An old enclosed bridge arching between brick buildings above a cobbled lane.
places.do: Frame the alley shot looking up Staple Street.
places.tip: A quick atmospheric detour on a Tribeca run.

places.name: New York Marble Cemetery
places.blurb: A hidden 1830s walled cemetery tucked inside an East Village block.
places.see: A secret green courtyard of marble vaults behind iron gates.
places.tip: Glimpse it through the gate; rarely open to the public.

places.name: Sherman Square
places.blurb: The bustling Upper West Side crossroads at Broadway and 72nd.
places.see: The landmark 1904 subway control house and streams of neighborhood life.
places.do: Cut a block west to enter Riverside Park.
places.tip: A natural turnaround point on a UWS run.

places.name: Duarte Square
places.blurb: A small triangular plaza where Tribeca meets SoHo.
places.see: Public murals and the Holland Tunnel traffic streaming nearby.
places.tip: Useful waypoint linking the Hudson path to SoHo.

places.name: Paley Park
places.blurb: A beloved Midtown 'pocket park' built around a waterfall wall.
places.see: A wall of cascading water muffling the city behind a curtain of honey locusts.
places.do: Stop for a breather inside the falling-water hush.
places.tip: A tiny oasis off Fifth Avenue; perfect cool-down spot.

places.name: Dante Park
places.blurb: A small triangle across from Lincoln Center.
places.see: A statue of Dante and the travertine arches of Lincoln Center opposite.
places.do: Cross to Lincoln Center's plaza and fountain.
places.tip: Quick pause near the UWS performing-arts hub.

places.name: Columbus Park
places.blurb: Chinatown's lively neighborhood park.
places.see: Morning tai chi, mahjong players, and the curve of historic courthouse domes nearby.
places.do: Soak up the local Chinatown street life around the edges.
places.tip: Most atmospheric in the early morning.

places.name: Central Park Conservatory Garden
places.blurb: Central Park's formal six-acre garden retreat.
places.see: Manicured French, Italian and English garden rooms with fountains and seasonal blooms.
places.do: Wander the Untermyer Fountain and wisteria pergola.
places.tip: Peak bloom in spring and fall; a quiet contrast to the loop drive.

places.name: JFK Promenade
places.blurb: Car-free main artery through Golden Gate Park.
places.see: A wide ribbon of pavement winding under towering eucalyptus and past museums, gardens, and the de Young's twisting tower.
places.do: Detour to the Conservatory of Flowers or the Japanese Tea Garden mid-run.
places.tip: Permanently car-free and dead flat—perfect for fast, uninterrupted miles any day.

places.name: Golden Gate Promenade / Crissy Field
places.blurb: SF's signature bayfront run beneath the Golden Gate Bridge.
places.see: The bridge looming over a restored tidal marsh, windsurfers skimming the bay, and Alcatraz floating offshore.
places.do: Finish with a flat lap to Fort Point directly under the bridge.
places.tip: Afternoons bring strong wind off the bay—run west-to-east for a tailwind home.

places.name: Herb Caen Way / The Embarcadero
places.blurb: The wide bayside boardwalk past the Ferry Building and piers.
places.see: Palm-lined promenade with the Bay Bridge arcing overhead, historic piers, and the Ferry Building clock tower.
places.do: Grab water or a snack at the Ferry Building marketplace at the midpoint.
places.tip: Flat and exposed; busy with tourists midday—go early for clear pavement.

places.name: Golden Gate Bridge Sidewalk
places.blurb: Run across the most famous bridge on the West Coast.
places.see: International-orange towers soaring above you, the open Pacific to the west, and the whole city skyline behind.
places.do: Cross to the Marin side and back, or continue down to Sausalito.
places.tip: Expect wind and fog; the east sidewalk is open to runners by day and gets crowded—start early.

places.name: Great Highway / Ocean Beach
places.blurb: Long, straight oceanfront path along the Pacific dunes.
places.see: Three miles of open Pacific surf, drifting sand, and big sky with the Sutro Tower behind you.
places.do: Drop onto the sand for a beach-running stretch beside the breakers.
places.tip: Often windy and foggy; the upper stretch is now a car-free promenade—flat the whole way.

places.name: Coastal Trail / Lands End
places.blurb: Cliff-edge trail with the wildest views in the city.
places.see: The Golden Gate framed by cypress, crashing surf far below, and shipwreck remnants at low tide.
places.do: Side-trip down to the Sutro Baths ruins and the Lands End Labyrinth.
places.tip: Rolling dirt-and-step trail with real climbs—trail shoes help; go at sunset for the best light.
places.transit: Lands End / Merrie Way (Muni 38 Geary to 38R)

places.name: Ocean Beach Esplanade
places.blurb: Paved seawall promenade at the north end of Ocean Beach.
places.see: A straight concrete esplanade above the sand with the Cliff House and Seal Rocks to the north.
places.do: Link north into the Sutro Heights and Lands End trails for a longer loop.
places.tip: Flat and fast but wind-exposed; pairs naturally with the Great Highway path.

places.name: Park Boulevard Trail
places.blurb: Wooded Presidio path above the western bluffs.
places.see: Shaded forest trail opening to ocean glimpses through the Monterey pines.
places.do: Connect to the Coastal Trail for a forest-to-cliff combination.
places.tip: Gentle grades on soft surface; quiet even on weekends.

places.name: Steep Ravine Trail
places.blurb: Short green trail in the hills near Tank Hill.
places.see: A leafy dirt path tucked into the slopes below Twin Peaks.
places.do: Climb to Tank Hill afterward for a panoramic city view.
places.tip: Short and steep—use it as a hill-repeat segment, not a destination.

places.name: Presidio Promenade
places.blurb: Tree-lined promenade through the heart of the Presidio.
places.see: Rows of historic barracks and parade-ground lawns under a canopy of cypress and pine.
places.do: Detour to the Presidio Tunnel Tops park for bridge-and-bay views.
places.tip: Mostly gentle with one short climb toward the bridge approach.

places.name: Sutro Heights Loop
places.blurb: Garden loop on the bluff above Ocean Beach.
places.see: Cypress-lined paths, old estate statuary, and a parapet overlook straight down the coast.
places.do: Stand at the stone overlook for the full Ocean Beach panorama.
places.tip: Tiny loop—best as a scenic add-on to a Lands End or Great Highway run.

places.name: Fulton Trail
places.blurb: Northern edge path of Golden Gate Park along Fulton Street.
places.see: A straight tree-shaded route bordering the park's wilder northern groves.
places.do: Cut south into the park's meadows or continue west toward Ocean Beach.
places.tip: Flat and direct—a good connector between the park and the coast.

places.name: Presidio Park Trail
places.blurb: Quiet forest trail in the Presidio interior.
places.see: Soft singletrack through dense pine and eucalyptus forest.
places.tip: Rolling and shaded; links easily to the Ecology and Park Boulevard trails.

places.name: Ecology Trail
places.blurb: Wooded climbing trail up through the Presidio forest.
places.see: A green dirt path winding past the Inspiration Point overlook and historic forest plantings.
places.do: Pause at Inspiration Point for a view over the bay and Angel Island.
places.tip: Steady uphill on the way out—good for hill work; soft underfoot.

places.name: Top of the Mark
places.blurb: Legendary Nob Hill sky lounge atop the Mark Hopkins.
places.see: A 360-degree panorama of the city, bay, and bridges from nineteen floors up.
places.do: Reward a hill run with a drink at the historic glass-walled bar.
places.tip: The climb up Nob Hill is steep from every direction—earn the view.
places.transit: Powell St (BART/Muni) then California cable car

places.name: The View Lounge
places.blurb: 39th-floor skyline lounge above Yerba Buena.
places.see: Sweeping downtown and bay views through dramatic angular windows.
places.tip: A good turnaround landmark on a downtown loop.

places.name: Bay Lights Viewpoint
places.blurb: Embarcadero spot facing the Bay Bridge light display.
places.see: The west span of the Bay Bridge strung with shimmering LED art over the water.
places.do: Time an evening run to catch the lights after dark.
places.tip: Best at night; sits right on the flat Embarcadero path.

places.name: Washington Square Park
places.blurb: North Beach's green heart beneath Saints Peter and Paul.
places.see: A lawn ringed by Italian cafes with the white spires of the church and Coit Tower behind.
places.do: Loop the park then climb toward Coit Tower on Telegraph Hill.
places.tip: Flat itself, but every route out climbs—North Beach is hilly.

places.name: Union Square
places.blurb: The city's grand central plaza and shopping crossroads.
places.see: A terraced granite square crowned by the Dewey Monument, framed by department stores and theaters.
places.do: Catch a cable car climbing past on the Powell Street line.
places.tip: Crowded by day—run through it early; downtown grid is mostly flat here.

places.name: Music Concourse
places.blurb: Sunken formal plaza at the cultural core of Golden Gate Park.
places.see: Pollarded plane trees, a tiered fountain, and the de Young and Academy of Sciences facing off across the bowl.
places.do: Circle the fountain then duck into the free-entry Academy garden or Tea Garden.
places.tip: Flat and central—an ideal pivot point for park loops.

places.name: Levi's Plaza
places.blurb: Landscaped fountain plaza at the foot of Telegraph Hill.
places.see: A stone-and-water park with a babbling granite fountain, brick HQ buildings, and the hill rising behind.
places.do: Climb the nearby Filbert Steps through the hidden gardens.
places.tip: Flat plaza, but the adjacent steps are a steep stair workout.

places.name: Filbert Steps
places.blurb: Famous garden stairway up Telegraph Hill to Coit Tower.
places.see: Wooden steps threading through lush private gardens, fig trees, and the wild parrots of Telegraph Hill.
places.do: Climb all the way to Coit Tower for the bay panorama.
places.tip: A genuine stair-climbing workout—steep and relentless to the top.

places.name: The Beat Museum
places.blurb: North Beach shrine to the Beat Generation.
places.see: Kerouac and Ginsberg memorabilia beside the legendary City Lights bookstore and Jack Kerouac Alley.
places.do: Wander Jack Kerouac Alley over to City Lights next door.
places.tip: A cultural pit stop on a flat North Beach–to–Chinatown route.

places.name: Cable Car Turntable (Powell & Market)
places.blurb: Where crews spin the Powell Street cable cars by hand.
places.see: Operators manually rotating a wooden cable car on its turntable amid a crowd of onlookers.
places.do: Watch a turn, then trace the cable line uphill toward Nob Hill.
places.tip: Always busy—a lively start point at the foot of downtown's hills.

places.name: Musée Mécanique
places.blurb: Antique arcade of penny machines on Fisherman's Wharf.
places.see: Hundreds of vintage coin-operated games and player pianos in a warehouse on Pier 45.
places.do: Drop a few quarters in the old machines mid-run.
places.tip: Right on the flat waterfront—an easy detour from the Embarcadero.

places.name: Japantown Peace Plaza
places.blurb: Cultural plaza centered on the Peace Pagoda.
places.see: The five-tiered concrete Peace Pagoda rising over a fountain plaza in the heart of Japantown.
places.do: Circle the pagoda then explore the Japan Center malls.
places.tip: Sits atop a modest rise west of downtown; flat once you arrive.

places.name: Bay Cruise Pier
places.blurb: Fisherman's Wharf launch point with open bay views.
places.see: Cruise boats heading out toward Alcatraz with the bay and bridges spread wide.
places.tip: A scenic waterfront turnaround at the north end of the Embarcadero.

places.name: Museo Italo Americano
places.blurb: Italian-American art museum at Fort Mason.
places.see: Rotating Italian art shows inside the historic Fort Mason piers above the bay.
places.do: Pair with a Fort Mason–to–Marina Green waterfront loop.
places.tip: Perched on the Fort Mason bluff between Aquatic Park and the Marina.

places.name: Museum of the African Diaspora
places.blurb: Downtown museum of the global African diaspora.
places.see: A striking glass facade with a multi-story photo mosaic of a child's face in Yerba Buena.
places.do: Continue into the Yerba Buena Gardens just across the street.
places.tip: Flat SoMa location—easy to fold into a downtown loop.

places.name: Harvey Milk Plaza
places.blurb: Castro landmark honoring the pioneering civil-rights leader.
places.see: A giant rainbow flag flying over the Castro Muni station at the neighborhood's symbolic gateway.
places.do: Run the rainbow crosswalks at Castro and 18th nearby.
places.tip: Gateway to the hilly Castro—flat at the plaza, steep just beyond.
places.transit: Castro Street Station (Muni Metro K, L, M)

places.name: St. Mary's Square
places.blurb: Quiet elevated green at the edge of Chinatown.
places.see: A lawn and the steel statue of Sun Yat-sen tucked above Old St. Mary's Cathedral.
places.do: Drop into Chinatown's Grant Avenue just downhill.
places.tip: A calm breather between the Financial District and Chinatown.

places.name: Willie "Woo Woo" Wong Park
places.blurb: Beloved community park in the core of Chinatown.
places.see: A terraced playground and courts buzzing with the rhythm of daily Chinatown life.
places.tip: Set on a Chinatown slope—short but steep streets all around.

places.name: War Memorial Court
places.blurb: Beaux-Arts courtyard in the Civic Center cultural district.
places.see: Symmetrical lawns between the Opera House and Veterans Building, with City Hall's gold dome nearby.
places.do: Loop around City Hall's grand plaza next door.
places.tip: Flat, formal, and open—handsome stretch of a Civic Center run.

places.name: Mary Ellen Pleasant Memorial Park
places.blurb: Tiny grove honoring a 19th-century Black entrepreneur and activist.
places.see: Six towering eucalyptus she planted, shading a quiet Pacific Heights corner.
places.tip: A brief historical pause on a hilly Pacific Heights route.

places.name: Mission Playground
places.blurb: Lively neighborhood park in the heart of the Mission.
places.see: Soccer pitch and pool busy with the energy of the Mission District.
places.tip: Flat Mission grid—useful as a sunny-side turnaround point.

places.name: Eureka Valley Recreation Center
places.blurb: Hillside rec center and green space below the Castro.
places.see: Open courts and lawn perched on the Eureka Valley slope.
places.tip: On a real grade—the surrounding streets make for steep intervals.
places.transit: Castro Street Station (Muni Metro K, L, M)

places.name: Bair Island Trail
places.blurb: A restored tidal marsh island minutes from downtown Redwood City.
places.see: Egrets and pelicans over the sloughs, salt-marsh flats, and the bay opening up past the levees.
places.do: Run the out-and-back levee path to the observation deck at the end.
places.tip: Zero shade and often windy — bring a cap.

places.name: Redwood Shores Lagoon & Bay Trail
places.blurb: Flat lagoon-side paths threading the Redwood Shores waterfront.
places.see: Glassy lagoons, rowers at dawn, the Oracle towers mirrored in the water, and Belmont Slough birdlife.
places.do: Link the lagoon loops to the open Bay Trail along the slough.

places.name: Seal Point & San Mateo Shoreline
places.blurb: San Mateo’s bayfront parkland on the open Bay Trail.
places.see: Kite-surfers off Seal Point, the San Mateo Bridge stretching to the East Bay, and miles of unbroken bay horizon.
places.do: Run the shoreline from Ryder Park toward Coyote Point.
places.tip: Afternoon winds are strong — run north-to-south on the way back.

places.name: Coyote Point Recreation Area
places.blurb: A wooded knoll jutting into the bay with a marina and beaches.
places.see: Eucalyptus groves, the small swimming beach, planes climbing out of SFO across the water.
places.do: Loop the point for the full panorama.

places.name: Foster City Levee Trail
places.blurb: The classic flat levee loop ringing Foster City.
places.see: Open bay on one side, lagoons and waterfront homes on the other, and the San Mateo Bridge head-on.
places.do: A favorite tempo-run circuit — pancake flat and car-free.

places.name: Palo Alto Baylands Nature Preserve
places.blurb: One of the bay’s best-preserved tidal marshes, laced with levee paths.
places.see: Boardwalks over pickleweed marsh, avocets and stilts working the mudflats, sailboats at the tiny harbor.
places.do: Run the levees out to the interpretive center boardwalk.
places.tip: Best at high tide for birdlife; bring sunglasses against the glare.

places.name: Bedwell Bayfront Park
places.blurb: Rolling reclaimed hills on the Menlo Park bayfront.
places.see: A 360° sweep from the bay across the whole Peninsula ridge line; harriers hunting the grassland.
places.do: Loop the perimeter and take the high knoll for the view.

places.name: Sawyer Camp Trail
places.blurb: The Peninsula’s marquee paved trail along Crystal Springs Reservoir.
places.see: Still blue reservoir water against forested watershed hills — protected land since the 1800s, and it shows.
places.do: An out-and-back along the water; the 600-year-old Jepson Laurel marks the halfway point.
places.tip: No services on the trail — carry water.
places.transit: Drive/bike to the Crystal Springs Rd gate

places.name: Cañada Road & Pulgas Water Temple
places.blurb: A country road shoulder path through oak-studded watershed meadows.
places.see: The Beaux-Arts Pulgas Water Temple — where Hetch Hetchy water arrives — framed by cypress and rolling grassland.
places.do: On Bicycle Sundays the whole road closes to cars.

places.name: Edgewood Park & Natural Preserve
places.blurb: Serpentine grassland famous for spring wildflowers.
places.see: Hillsides of goldfields and poppies in March–May, oak woodland, and ridge views back over the bay.
places.do: The Serpentine Loop is a runnable 3-mile dirt circuit.
places.tip: Trails are dirt singletrack — watch your footing.

places.name: Emerald Hills & Handley Rock
places.blurb: Winding lanes and a sandstone outcrop high above Redwood City.
places.see: From the rock: the whole South Bay laid out, from the Dumbarton to Mount Diablo on a clear day.
places.do: A stout hill workout — the climb up Jefferson earns the view.
places.tip: Quiet residential streets with no sidewalks in places; run aware.

places.name: Stulsaft Park
places.blurb: A surprise canyon of oaks and creek trails inside Redwood City.
places.see: Forty wooded acres of dirt paths, a seasonal creek, and shady switchbacks.
places.do: Cut through it to link downtown with the Farm Hill climb.

places.name: Water Dog Lake Park
places.blurb: A pocket reservoir tucked in the Belmont hills.
places.see: A green lake bowl ringed by chaparral trails, with bay glimpses from the upper fire road.
places.do: The climb from Lyall Way is short and rewarding.

places.name: The Stanford Dish
places.blurb: The iconic paved loop through golden foothills to the radio telescope.
places.see: The Dish itself, grazing cattle, ground squirrels everywhere, and a horizon from San Francisco to San Jose.
places.do: The full loop from the Stanford Ave gate is the Peninsula’s signature hill run.
places.tip: Gates close at sunset; no water on the loop.

places.name: Courthouse Square
places.blurb: Redwood City’s 1910 domed courthouse and its lively plaza.
places.see: The glass-domed San Mateo County History Museum, outdoor movie nights, and the “Climate Best By Government Test” arch.
places.do: The natural start/finish line for a downtown run.

places.name: Mezes Park
places.blurb: A small hillside green a few blocks above downtown Redwood City.
places.see: Old-Redwood-City bungalows on the climb up, and rooftops of the downtown core below.
places.do: A quick warm-up loop before heading for the hills or the bay.

places.name: Red Morton Community Park
places.blurb: Redwood City’s big backyard of fields, courts, and loops.
places.see: The Magical Bridge playground, ballfields, and a steady stream of local runners on the perimeter path.
places.do: Lap the perimeter to pad a short downtown loop.

places.name: Stafford Park
places.blurb: A gracious palm-ringed green in Redwood City’s old quarter.
places.see: Craftsman bungalows and mature palms on the surrounding blocks of Edgewood and Hopkins.

places.name: Laurel Street, San Carlos
places.blurb: The City of Good Living’s walkable, café-lined main street.
places.see: A classic small-downtown strip with the 1917 Caltrain depot at its foot.
places.do: A mid-run espresso stop if you’re honest with your splits.

places.name: Twin Pines Park
places.blurb: A creekside woodland park behind downtown Belmont.
places.see: Redwood groves along Belmont Creek and the city’s little sculpture garden.

places.name: Central Park, San Mateo
places.blurb: San Mateo’s formal downtown park with a celebrated Japanese garden.
places.see: The koi pond and granite pagoda of the Japanese Tea Garden, rose beds, and the mini railroad.
places.do: Start here and you’re three blocks from downtown’s ramen row.

places.name: Downtown San Mateo (B Street)
places.blurb: The Peninsula’s best eating street, three blocks long.
places.see: B Street’s ramen shops and bakeries, the old Wisnom’s hardware façade, and the Caltrain depot.

places.name: Holbrook-Palmer Park
places.blurb: An estate-turned-park under Atherton’s legendary tree canopy.
places.see: Great lawns, a Victorian water tower, and streets of fabled quiet on every side.
places.do: Atherton’s shaded lanes are some of the gentlest miles around.

places.name: Santa Cruz Avenue, Menlo Park
places.blurb: Menlo Park’s tidy, tree-lined downtown strip.
places.see: Bookstores, bakeries, and the 1867 rail depot — the oldest continuously operating station in California.

places.name: Burgess Park & San Francisquito Creek
places.blurb: Menlo Park’s civic green beside the creek that divides two counties.
places.see: The creek corridor’s oaks and the sports fields where half the town seems to be at any hour.
places.do: Pick up the creek-side streets toward Palo Alto.

places.name: Stanford Campus & Palm Drive
places.blurb: The grand axis of palms leading to the sandstone Main Quad.
places.see: Palm Drive’s mile of Canary palms, Memorial Church’s mosaics, the Oval, and Rodin bronzes by the art museum.
places.do: Loop the Quad arcades — running them at dawn is a rite of passage.
places.tip: Campus paths are bike-heavy at class change times.

places.name: Hoover Tower
places.blurb: Stanford’s 285-foot campanile, visible from everywhere on campus.
places.see: The carillon tower over the red-tile roofs; the observation deck sees three counties.
places.do: Round it past the Quad arcades and White Plaza.

places.name: Lake Lagunita
places.blurb: Stanford’s seasonal lake bed ringed by a soft dirt loop.
places.see: Tidewater grasses, the foothills rising behind, and salamander fences in the wet months.
places.do: The lake-bed loop is the campus’s favorite easy mile.

places.name: University Avenue, Palo Alto
places.blurb: The downtown street where a startup myth lives behind every façade.
places.see: The 1929 Stanford Theatre marquee, sidewalk cafés, and the gateway arch toward the campus.

places.name: Professorville
places.blurb: Palo Alto’s historic district of shingled 1890s faculty homes.
places.see: Brown-shingle Craftsman houses under giant oaks — including the HP garage birthplace a few blocks over on Addison.

places.name: Eleanor Pardee Park & Crescent Park
places.blurb: A garden park at the edge of Palo Alto’s grandest old neighborhood.
places.see: Crescent Park’s magnolia-lined avenues and storybook houses.

places.name: Bol Park Path
places.blurb: A bike path through Barron Park, home of Palo Alto’s donkeys.
places.see: The resident donkey pasture (say hi to Perry’s successors), Matadero Creek, and garden backyards.
places.do: Link it toward the Stanford Research Park loop.

places.name: Charles River Esplanade
places.blurb: Boston's signature riverside running path along the Charles.
places.see: The full sweep of the Charles, sailboats out on the basin, and the Back Bay skyline glowing across the water at dusk.
places.do: Loop one of the footbridges over Storrow Drive to add the lagoon islands and the Hatch Shell.
places.tip: Run it early; the riverside fills with cyclists and rowers by mid-morning.

places.name: Boston HarborWalk
places.blurb: Waterfront promenade tracing Boston Harbor through the Seaport.
places.see: Open harbor on one side, gleaming Seaport towers on the other, with ferries and water taxis cutting across the channel.
places.do: Detour onto the Fan Pier and Seaport Common plazas for harbor-level views.
places.tip: Wind off the water can be biting; layer up even on mild days.

places.name: Boston HarborWalk (Fort Point)
places.blurb: HarborWalk segment along the Fort Point Channel.
places.see: Still channel water reflecting old brick wharf buildings and the converted warehouses of the Fort Point arts district.
places.do: Cross a channel bridge to link up with the Seaport HarborWalk.

places.name: Public Garden Lagoon Path
places.blurb: Loop around the lagoon at the heart of the Public Garden.
places.see: The willow-draped lagoon, the little suspension bridge, and the Swan Boats gliding past beds of tulips.
places.do: Circle the lagoon then connect across Charles St into Boston Common.
places.tip: A gentle, flat warmup loop before a longer Esplanade run.

places.name: Muddy River Path (Emerald Necklace)
places.blurb: Emerald Necklace path tracing the Muddy River past the Fens.
places.see: Reedy riverbanks and weeping willows winding through Olmsted's chain of green between Fenway and the Riverway.
places.do: Follow it south to link the Back Bay Fens with the Riverway and Jamaica Pond.
places.tip: Quiet and shaded; a good escape from city traffic.

places.name: Emerald Necklace (Riverway)
places.blurb: Wooded Riverway stretch of Olmsted's Emerald Necklace.
places.see: A sunken green ribbon of footpaths and stone bridges that feels miles from the city it threads through.
places.tip: Connects seamlessly to the Muddy River path heading north.

places.name: Back Bay Fens Path
places.blurb: Path winding through the Back Bay Fens of the Emerald Necklace.
places.see: Marshy reed beds, the historic Victory Gardens, and stone-arched Agassiz Road framing the green.
places.do: Loop the Fens then head west on the Muddy River toward the Riverway.

places.name: Mayor's Walk (Commonwealth Ave Mall)
places.blurb: Tree-lined mall promenade through Back Bay.
places.see: A grand European-style allee of elms and statuary running down the spine of Commonwealth Avenue's brownstones.
places.do: Run the full Comm Ave Mall west toward the Fens or east to the Public Garden.
places.tip: Magnolias bloom along the side streets in early spring.

places.name: North End Waterfront (Commercial Street)
places.blurb: HarborWalk stretch along the North End's working waterfront.
places.see: Old wharves and the marina at the foot of the North End, with the harbor opening out past Christopher Columbus Park.
places.do: Cut inland a block for an espresso on Hanover Street.

places.name: North Washington Street Bridge
places.blurb: River crossing linking the North End to Charlestown.
places.see: The mouth of the Charles where it meets the harbor, with the Zakim Bridge cables soaring just upstream.
places.do: Cross into Charlestown to pick up the Navy Yard and Bunker Hill.

places.name: Cambridge Parkway Path
places.blurb: Riverside path along the Cambridge bank near the dam.
places.see: The Charles basin from the north shore, with the Boston skyline stacked up across the water.
places.do: Connect over the Museum of Science dam to reach the Esplanade.

places.name: North Bank Bridge HarborWalk
places.blurb: Footbridge HarborWalk link between the North End and Charlestown.
places.see: A curving pedestrian bridge over the locks where the river spills into the harbor.

places.name: Somerville Community Path
places.blurb: Rail-trail running path through Somerville.
places.see: A leafy, car-free greenway threading neighborhoods, murals, and the new Green Line viaduct.
places.do: Follow it west toward Davis Square and the Minuteman trail.
places.tip: Flat and uninterrupted, ideal for steady tempo miles.

places.name: Skywalk Observatory
places.blurb: 360-degree observation deck atop the Prudential Tower.
places.see: All of Boston laid out below: the Charles, the harbor islands, and Fenway's lights on a clear evening.
places.do: Cool down here after a Back Bay run for the citywide panorama.
places.tip: Ticketed and indoors; a destination rather than a running stop.

places.name: Boston Public Garden
places.blurb: America's first public botanical garden, beside Boston Common.
places.see: Victorian flower beds, the Make Way for Ducklings statues, and Swan Boats on the willow-rimmed lagoon.
places.do: Lap the lagoon then cross into the Common for a longer loop.
places.tip: Paths are gravel and crowded midday; run the perimeter early.

places.name: Boston Common
places.blurb: The oldest public park in America and start of the Freedom Trail.
places.see: Rolling lawns, the Soldiers and Sailors Monument on Flagstaff Hill, and the gold-domed State House above the treeline.
places.do: Pick up the red-brick Freedom Trail line here and follow it toward the North End.
places.tip: Frog Pond becomes a skating rink in winter.

places.name: Freedom Trail
places.blurb: Red-brick line linking 16 of Boston's Revolutionary sites.
places.see: A 2.5-mile thread of history past the State House, Granary Burying Ground, Old North Church, and on to Bunker Hill.
places.do: Run it end to end from the Common to Charlestown as a self-guided history tour.
places.tip: Follow the brick line embedded in the sidewalk; no map needed.

places.name: Rose Kennedy Greenway
places.blurb: Linear park where the elevated Central Artery once stood.
places.see: A 1.5-mile chain of fountains, gardens, and public art running from Chinatown to the North End.
places.do: Run its length to connect the Common, the Greenway, and the harbor.
places.tip: Cooling fountains run in summer; great for a hot-day finish.

places.name: North End Parks (Greenway)
places.blurb: Greenway parks at the gateway to the North End.
places.see: Pergolas and lawns framing a clean sightline to the Custom House Tower and the harbor.
places.tip: Steps from Hanover Street's cafes and the Freedom Trail.

places.name: Custom House Tower
places.blurb: Landmark clock tower with an observation deck over the harbor.
places.see: Boston's first skyscraper rising above the old wharf district, its illuminated clock a fixed point on the skyline.
places.tip: A useful navigation landmark on harbor and Greenway runs.

places.name: Central Wharf (New England Aquarium)
places.blurb: Harborfront plaza around the New England Aquarium.
places.see: Working wharves, the harbor ferry docks, and seals basking in the Aquarium's outdoor tank.
places.do: Pick up the HarborWalk here heading north or south along the water.

places.name: Copley Square
places.blurb: Grand Back Bay plaza ringed by landmark architecture.
places.see: Richardson's Trinity Church mirrored in the glass Hancock Tower, with the Boston Public Library across the square.
places.do: Stand on the Boston Marathon finish line painted on nearby Boylston Street.
places.tip: A weekly farmers market fills the plaza in season.

places.name: Granary Burying Ground
places.blurb: 1660 graveyard on the Freedom Trail.
places.see: Weathered slate headstones over the graves of Paul Revere, John Hancock, and Samuel Adams.
places.tip: A natural pause on a Freedom Trail run.

places.name: Acorn Street, Beacon Hill
places.blurb: The most photographed cobblestone lane in America.
places.see: A narrow, gaslit cobblestone street of brick rowhouses and flower boxes climbing Beacon Hill.
places.do: Wind through Beacon Hill's hilly lanes up to the State House.
places.tip: Cobbles are uneven; watch your footing and go gently.

places.name: Faneuil Hall Marketplace
places.blurb: Historic market and meeting hall, the 'Cradle of Liberty.'
places.see: The colonial brick hall and the long granite Quincy Market arcade buzzing with street performers and vendors.
places.tip: Dense pedestrian crowds midday; pass through early or detour via the Greenway.

places.name: North End
places.blurb: Boston's historic Italian neighborhood of narrow streets.
places.see: Tight brick lanes, the Paul Revere House, and Old North Church's white steeple above the rooftops.
places.do: Thread Hanover and Salem Streets, then finish on the harbor HarborWalk.
places.tip: Reward the miles with a cannoli; the bakery lines move fast in the morning.

places.name: Charlestown Navy Yard & USS Constitution
places.blurb: Historic naval shipyard home to 'Old Ironsides.'
places.see: The masts of USS Constitution, the oldest commissioned warship afloat, against the harbor and downtown skyline.
places.do: Run the Navy Yard HarborWalk and climb to the Bunker Hill Monument above.
places.tip: Across the river in Charlestown; reachable via the North Washington bridge.

places.name: Bunker Hill Monument
places.blurb: 221-foot granite obelisk marking the 1775 battle.
places.see: A commanding hilltop obelisk with sweeping views over Charlestown, the harbor, and the Boston skyline.
places.do: Climb the 294 interior steps for the view, then run back down to the Navy Yard.
places.tip: The hill itself is a stiff climb; a worthy turnaround point.

places.name: Castle Island
places.blurb: Harborside fort and beach loop in South Boston.
places.see: Fort Independence's granite walls, planes banking into Logan across the water, and the open Atlantic beyond.
places.do: Run the Pleasure Bay causeway loop around the lagoon and out to the fort.
places.tip: Sullivan's window has the classic post-run hot dog; the loop is flat and exposed.

places.name: Fenway Park
places.blurb: The oldest ballpark in Major League Baseball, opened 1912.
places.see: The looming green wall of the Green Monster and Yawkey Way's brick facade just off Kenmore Square.
places.do: Loop the park exterior and continue into the Back Bay Fens next door.
places.tip: Avoid game-day evenings; the streets jam with fans.

places.name: BU Beach
places.blurb: Grassy riverside knoll along the BU campus.
places.see: A sloping lawn between Storrow Drive and the Charles, popular with students sprawled in the sun.
places.do: Step onto the adjacent Esplanade path to run along the river.

places.name: Cambridge Common
places.blurb: Historic green near Harvard Square.
places.see: Shaded paths and Revolutionary War memorials where Washington once mustered the Continental Army.
places.do: Use it as a turnaround for runs out to Harvard from the river.

places.name: Christopher Columbus Waterfront Park
places.blurb: Harborfront park with a signature rose-covered trellis.
places.see: A long wisteria-draped pergola opening onto the marina and the harbor beyond.
places.do: Connect the North End HarborWalk to the Greenway here.

places.name: Hatch Shell & Music Oval
places.blurb: Riverside amphitheater lawn on the Esplanade.
places.see: The Art Deco band shell facing a broad green oval, with the Charles and Cambridge skyline behind it.
places.do: A natural rest or turnaround on an Esplanade run; July 4th fireworks launch from here.

places.name: Statler Park
places.blurb: Small landscaped square at the edge of Bay Village.
places.see: A quiet brick-bordered green with mature trees tucked between Park Plaza and the theater district.
places.tip: Handy connector between the Public Garden and the South End.

places.name: Charles Street, Beacon Hill
places.blurb: Antique-shop spine at the foot of Beacon Hill.
places.see: Gas lamps, brick sidewalks, and bow-front shops linking the Common to the Charles River.
places.do: Run it from the Public Garden up into Beacon Hill toward Acorn Street.

places.name: Seaport Common
places.blurb: Modern plaza-park at the heart of the Seaport District.
places.see: Open lawn and public art ringed by glass towers, a block from the harbor's edge.
places.do: Step onto the Seaport HarborWalk from here for the waterfront.

places.name: Lakefront Trail
places.blurb: Chicago’s legendary path along the Lake Michigan shore — 18 miles of open water and skyline.
places.see: The skyline stacked against the lake, beaches and harbors, and sailboats out on the blue.
places.do: Run the separated pedestrian lane north past the beaches or south to the Museum Campus.
places.tip: Separated run and bike paths most of the way; the lake wind can flip your effort on the return.

places.name: Chicago Riverwalk
places.blurb: A continuous promenade down at the water on the main branch of the Chicago River.
places.see: The river’s movable bridges overhead, the Marina City “corncobs,” and tour boats gliding past architecture.
places.do: Run the full Riverwalk from the lake to Lake Street, dipping under each bridge.
places.tip: Floods to the rail in high water; lively with bars and boats on summer evenings.

places.name: The 606 (Bloomingdale Trail)
places.blurb: An elevated rail-trail park running through the northwest-side neighborhoods.
places.see: Prairie plantings and art along an old freight line, with rooftop-level views over Wicker Park and Humboldt Park.
places.do: Run the full 2.7-mile viaduct end to end, above the street grid the whole way.
places.tip: Car-free and flat — a rare uninterrupted stretch away from the lake.

places.name: Lincoln Park Paths
places.blurb: Winding paths through the city’s largest lakefront park.
places.see: Lily ponds and the free zoo, the conservatory, and the skyline framed across South Pond.
places.do: Loop the park’s ponds and lawns, then drop onto the Lakefront Trail alongside.

places.name: Navy Pier Flyover
places.blurb: An elevated section of the Lakefront Trail bypassing the Navy Pier crowds.
places.see: Bird’s-eye views over the river mouth, Ogden Slip, and the lake from the raised deck.
places.do: Use it to run the lakefront straight past Navy Pier without the foot traffic.

places.name: Museum Campus
places.blurb: A lakefront park ringing Chicago’s trio of grand museums.
places.see: The Field Museum, Shedd Aquarium, and Adler Planetarium, with a postcard skyline view from the planetarium point.
places.do: Run out to the Adler’s lakefront point for the best skyline-and-water photo in the city.

places.name: Dearborn Street Bikeway
places.blurb: A protected two-way path straight through the Loop.
places.see: The Picasso sculpture at Daley Plaza, the County Building, and the Loop’s canyon of towers.
places.do: A direct north–south spine across downtown linking the river to Printers Row.

places.name: Milwaukee Avenue Bikeway
places.blurb: The diagonal artery through the hip near-northwest side.
places.see: Murals, taquerias, and vintage storefronts running from the river out to Wicker Park.
places.do: A street-level link from downtown toward the 606.

places.name: Ping Tom Park Riverwalk
places.blurb: A riverside park and walk on the South Branch in Chinatown.
places.see: A red pavilion and pagoda-style bridge, willow banks, and the river curving toward downtown.
places.do: A quieter riverside loop south of the Loop.

places.name: Millennium Park
places.blurb: Chicago’s showpiece park, home to “The Bean.”
places.see: Cloud Gate’s mirrored curve, the Pritzker Pavilion’s steel ribbons, and the faces of Crown Fountain.
places.do: Loop the park and cross the snaking BP Bridge into Maggie Daley Park next door.
places.tip: Mobbed at the Bean by day; run through at dawn to have the mirror to yourself.

places.name: 360 Chicago (Hancock)
places.blurb: The observation deck near the top of the former John Hancock Center.
places.see: The lake, the skyline, and four states on a clear day — plus the stomach-dropping TILT windows.
places.do: A landmark finish on a Magnificent Mile run.
places.tip: Ticketed and indoors; a destination rather than a running stop.

places.name: Navy Pier (Polk Bros Park)
places.blurb: The gateway park at the foot of Navy Pier on the lakefront.
places.see: The pier’s Centennial Wheel, a performing fountain, and the lake opening east past the breakwater.
places.do: Run out along the pier for open-water views, then rejoin the Lakefront Trail.

places.name: Willis Tower & Wacker
places.blurb: The foot of the tower that was North America’s tallest for a generation.
places.see: The black-steel Willis (Sears) Tower soaring overhead, with the river and Wacker Drive alongside.
places.do: A Loop landmark linking the Riverwalk to the Dearborn bikeway.

places.name: Water Tower & Byrne Plaza
places.blurb: The limestone Water Tower that survived the Great Chicago Fire.
places.see: The castellated 1869 tower marooned among the Magnificent Mile’s high-rises, with a plaza alongside.
places.do: A historic waypoint on a Michigan Avenue run.

places.name: Art Institute South Garden
places.blurb: A sunken garden room beside the Art Institute on Michigan Avenue.
places.see: A Hedge of honey locusts around the Fountain of the Great Lakes, walled off from the street noise.
places.do: A shaded pause between Millennium Park and the museum’s bronze lions.

places.name: Pritzker Park
places.blurb: A small Loop park across from the Harold Washington Library.
places.see: Trees and seating inspired by a Magritte painting, tucked into the South Loop edge.

places.name: Printers Row Park
places.blurb: A slender triangle park in the historic Printers Row district.
places.see: The landmark Dearborn Station clock tower closing the view down the street.

places.name: Haymarket Memorial
places.blurb: A monument marking the site of the 1886 Haymarket Affair.
places.see: A bronze sculpture on a speaker’s-wagon plinth where the rally for the eight-hour day turned tragic.
places.do: A labor-history stop on a West Loop / river run.

places.name: Chicago City Hall Roof Garden
places.blurb: One of the city’s pioneering green roofs, atop City Hall in the Loop.
places.see: A planted prairie roof (glimpsed from neighboring towers) that helped launch Chicago’s green-roof movement.
places.do: A landmark to note in passing through the Loop — the roof itself is not open to the public.

places.name: Grandmother’s Garden
places.blurb: A historic perennial garden in north Lincoln Park.
places.see: Informal beds of native perennials, one of the oldest public gardens in the city, by the Lincoln statue.
places.do: A pretty turnaround on a north Lincoln Park run.

places.name: Lincoln Park Conservatory Gardens
places.blurb: Formal gardens beside the Victorian glasshouse in Lincoln Park.
places.see: A grand Beaux-Arts garden, the conservatory’s glass domes, and seasonal flower shows.
places.do: Pair with the zoo and pond paths on a Lincoln Park loop.

places.name: American Writers Museum
places.blurb: A museum of American literature on Michigan Avenue.
places.see: Interactive galleries celebrating the nation’s writers, across from Millennium Park.

places.name: Ann and Roy Butler Hike-and-Bike Trail
places.blurb: Austin’s beloved 10-mile loop around the shores of Lady Bird Lake.
places.see: The downtown skyline mirrored in the water, paddleboarders and rowers, and the Pfluger and Lamar pedestrian bridges.
places.do: Run the full loop, crossing the lake on the boardwalk over the water on the south-east side.
places.tip: Shaded and crowded at dawn and dusk; the over-water boardwalk near I-35 is the highlight.

places.name: Barton Creek Greenbelt
places.blurb: A rugged limestone creek trail winding into the green hills southwest of downtown.
places.see: Cliffs and swimming holes, cypress-shaded creek crossings, and rock climbers on the bluffs.
places.do: Run the Violet Crown Trail from Zilker out along the creek and back.
places.tip: Rooty and rocky — trail shoes help, and the creek can run high after rain.

places.name: Shoal Creek Trail
places.blurb: A creekside greenway running north from Lady Bird Lake through central Austin.
places.see: Limestone creek banks, Pease Park’s big oaks, and quiet stretches just blocks from downtown.
places.do: Link the lake trail with Pease Park on an out-and-back up the creek.

places.name: Waller Creek Trail
places.blurb: A revitalized creek path threading the east side of downtown.
places.see: New creekside parks and boardwalks linking the Convention Center toward the lake.

places.name: Boggy Creek Greenbelt
places.blurb: A green creekside corridor through historic East Austin.
places.see: Neighborhood gardens, ball fields, and shaded creek banks away from the crowds.

places.name: Johnson Creek Trail
places.blurb: A short connector trail running up from the lake on the west side.
places.see: A leafy creek route linking the Butler trail toward the MoPac corridor.
places.do: Use it to extend the lake loop northwest.

places.name: Red Line Trail
places.blurb: An urban rail-trail shadowing the CapMetro Red Line east of downtown.
places.see: Murals and warehouses through the East Austin arts district.
places.do: A flat, straight option linking Plaza Saltillo toward the lake.

places.name: UT Main Mall
places.blurb: The ceremonial heart of the University of Texas campus.
places.see: The UT Tower above the fountains and live oaks, with the South Mall framing the Capitol view.
places.do: Run the Mall, then loop the campus and down to Waller Creek.

places.name: Auditorium Shores
places.blurb: The open lakefront lawn with the best downtown skyline view in Austin.
places.see: The full skyline across the water, the Stevie Ray Vaughan statue, and a big off-leash dog field.
places.do: A natural start/finish for the lake loop; catch the bats from the nearby Congress bridge at dusk.

places.name: Doug Sahm Hill
places.blurb: A gentle grassy summit in Butler Park overlooking the lake.
places.see: A 360° view of the skyline, the lake, and the Hill Country rolling off to the west.
places.do: A short, punchy climb just off the lake trail for the best free overlook downtown.

places.name: Lou Neff Point
places.blurb: A scenic lookout where Barton Creek meets Lady Bird Lake.
places.see: A little gazebo, the lake opening toward the skyline, and Zilker Park spreading behind.
places.do: A pretty turn on the lake loop and the gateway to Barton Springs.

places.name: Texas State Capitol Grounds
places.blurb: The grounds of the towering pink-granite Texas Capitol.
places.see: The dome rising above live oaks and monuments, taller than the U.S. Capitol in Washington.
places.do: Run the Capitol grounds, then take the Congress Avenue axis down toward the lake.

places.name: Willie Nelson Statue
places.blurb: A bronze of Austin’s patron saint of country music, downtown.
places.see: Willie and his guitar Trigger outside ACL Live, on the street named for him.
places.do: A quick photo stop in the 2nd Street District.

places.name: Republic Square
places.blurb: A historic downtown square shaded by sprawling heritage oaks.
places.see: The “Auction Oaks” where Austin’s lots were first sold, ringed by farmers-market stalls on weekends.

places.name: Brush Square
places.blurb: A leafy downtown square preserving two of Austin’s oldest houses.
places.see: The O. Henry and Susanna Dickinson museum cottages under the trees.

places.name: Kingsbury Commons at Pease Park
places.blurb: The revitalized lower end of Pease Park along Shoal Creek.
places.see: Restored lawns, a treehouse and splash play area, and the creek under big oaks.
places.do: A green anchor on the Shoal Creek Trail.

places.name: Texas State Cemetery
places.blurb: A quiet, history-steeped cemetery in East Austin.
places.see: The graves of Stephen F. Austin and Texas statesmen, with a reflecting pond and live oaks.
places.do: A calm, contemplative loop off the East Austin trails.

places.name: Seaholm Waterfront
places.blurb: A reclaimed lakefront beside the old Seaholm power plant.
places.see: The restored Art Deco power station, new plazas, and the lake trail running past.
places.do: A modern downtown link between the library, the lake, and Shoal Creek.

places.name: The Color Inside (Turrell Skyspace)
places.blurb: A James Turrell skyspace crowning the UT student center.
places.see: An open oculus to the sky framed by shifting light — best at sunset.
places.do: A rooftop art detour on a campus run.
places.tip: Free, but the sunset light sequence is worth timing your run around.

places.name: Angelina Eberly Statue
places.blurb: A lively bronze of the woman who fired a cannon to keep Austin the capital.
places.see: Angelina mid-blast at the cannon she used in the 1842 “Archive War,” on Congress Avenue.
places.do: A fun downtown photo stop on the Congress Avenue axis.

places.name: Country Club Creek Trail
places.blurb: A creekside greenway through the fast-changing east side.
places.see: Quiet creek banks and neighborhood greenery linking toward the lake’s southeast shore.
places.do: Use it to extend the lake loop into East Riverside.

places.name: Woodland Trail
places.blurb: A wooded connector off the south shore of Lady Bird Lake.
places.see: Shaded creek and woodland just back from the lake near the Norwood estate.
places.do: A leafy spur off the south side of the Butler trail.

places.name: Hirshfeld House
places.blurb: An ornate Victorian home from Austin’s early downtown days.
places.see: Gingerbread trim and a wrought-iron fence on a leafy block west of Congress.

places.name: Rickenbacker Causeway Trail
places.blurb: The wide bayside path arcing across the water toward Key Biscayne.
places.see: Open Biscayne Bay, the downtown skyline behind you, sailboarders, and the rise of the William Powell Bridge.
places.do: Run out over the bridge for the skyline view, with Hobie Beach and Virginia Key beyond.
places.tip: Exposed and windy with no shade — go early and carry water; the bridge is the one real hill in Miami.

places.name: Brickell Bay Walk
places.blurb: A baywalk threading between Brickell’s glass towers and the water.
places.see: Biscayne Bay, luxury high-rises, and yachts moored along the seawall.
places.do: Connect north to the Miami River and downtown’s Bayfront Park.
places.tip: A few private-property gaps still break the path; detour a block inland where it ends.

places.name: South Beach Beachwalk (Lummus Park)
places.blurb: The beachfront promenade along the sand of South Beach.
places.see: Pastel Art Deco hotels on Ocean Drive, palm groves, lifeguard towers, and the Atlantic surf.
places.do: Run the beachwalk past the Deco District and on toward South Pointe.

places.name: Miami Beach Boardwalk
places.blurb: A continuous beachfront boardwalk running up the Mid-Beach dunes.
places.see: Sea-grape and dune plantings, grand oceanfront hotels, and uninterrupted Atlantic views.
places.do: A long, flat, car-free stretch — ideal for tempo miles north from South Beach.

places.name: South Pointe Park
places.blurb: The green southern tip of Miami Beach where the bay meets the ocean.
places.see: Cruise ships sliding through Government Cut, the South Pointe Pier, and skyline views across the water.
places.do: Loop the park paths and run the pier out over the channel.

places.name: MacArthur Causeway Baywalk
places.blurb: The bayside path along the main causeway between downtown and South Beach.
places.see: The Port of Miami’s cruise terminals, the mansions of Star Island, and the bay on both sides.
places.do: A long water crossing linking the mainland to Miami Beach.
places.tip: Traffic-side and exposed — best as a point-to-point, not a there-and-back.

places.name: Virginia Key North Point Trails
places.blurb: Sandy nature and mountain-bike trails on a barrier island off the causeway.
places.see: Mangroves, hammock forest, quiet beaches, and skyline glimpses across the bay.
places.do: Trade pavement for soft singletrack just minutes from downtown.

places.name: Miami Riverwalk
places.blurb: A downtown promenade along the historic Miami River.
places.see: Working fishing boats and drawbridges, riverside restaurants, and the towers of the financial district.
places.do: Trace the river inland from the bay to link Brickell and downtown.

places.name: Commodore Trail
places.blurb: A shaded path running south toward leafy Coconut Grove.
places.see: Banyan canopies, bayfront estates, and the village edge of the Grove.
places.do: Head south to Vizcaya and the Grove’s marinas.

places.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
places.blurb: A Gilded-Age Italian villa and formal gardens on the edge of the bay.
places.see: Baroque fountains and clipped hedges, the stone barge breakwater, and the villa above Biscayne Bay.
places.do: A landmark turnaround at the south end of a bayfront run.
places.tip: Gardens are ticketed; a passing landmark unless you stop in.

places.name: South Pointe Park Pier
places.blurb: A curving pier at the southern tip of Miami Beach.
places.see: Cruise ships and freighters threading Government Cut, with the skyline and Fisher Island across the water.
places.do: Run the pier as the turnaround on a South Beach loop.

places.name: Maurice A. Ferré Park (Museum Park)
places.blurb: A waterfront park downtown framing two of Miami’s signature museums.
places.see: The Pérez Art Museum’s hanging gardens, the domed Frost science museum, and the bay beyond.
places.do: A green anchor between the downtown baywalk and the causeways.

places.name: The Underline
places.blurb: A linear park and path unfurling beneath the Metrorail tracks.
places.see: Native gardens, murals, and public art running south from Brickell along the transit line.
places.do: A shaded, car-free spine connecting Brickell toward Coconut Grove.

places.name: Miami Circle at Brickell Point
places.blurb: A prehistoric Tequesta site carved in the bedrock at the river mouth.
places.see: The circular archaeological ring on a small bayfront lawn where the Miami River meets the bay.
places.do: A quick history stop at the start of the Brickell baywalk.

places.name: José Martí Park
places.blurb: A riverfront park at the gateway to Little Havana.
places.see: Royal palms and a riverside walk where downtown meets the Cuban-American heart of the city.
places.do: Pick up the Miami Riverwalk here heading toward the bay.

places.name: Belle Isle Park
places.blurb: A small island park at the foot of the Venetian Causeway.
places.see: A baywalk circling the island with open views back to the Miami Beach skyline.
places.do: Loop the island as a quiet detour off the Venetian Causeway run.

places.name: Collins Park
places.blurb: A cultural green in South Beach beside the Bass Museum.
places.see: Sculpture on the lawn, the Bass contemporary-art museum, and the library, a block from the sand.

places.name: Miami Beach Botanical Garden
places.blurb: A lush pocket garden in the heart of Miami Beach.
places.see: Palms, orchids, and a lily pond with the Convention Center alongside.

places.name: Ichimura Miami-Japan Garden
places.blurb: A serene Japanese garden on Watson Island in the bay.
places.see: Koi ponds, stone lanterns, and raked gravel framed by downtown towers across the water.
places.do: A calm detour off the MacArthur Causeway.

places.name: Alice Wainwright Park
places.blurb: A bayfront park on the rise toward Coconut Grove.
places.see: Hardwood hammock, a rare ridge of limestone, and open bay views toward Key Biscayne.
places.do: A green waypoint on the Commodore Trail south of Brickell.

places.name: Maurice Gibb Memorial Park
places.blurb: A small waterfront park on the Sunset Harbour bayfront.
places.see: A short baywalk and dock with views over the marina and the Venetian islands.

places.name: Victoria Embankment
places.blurb: A grand riverside boulevard along the north bank of the Thames.
places.see: Cleopatra’s Needle, the sphinxes and dolphin lamps, and the London Eye turning across the water.
places.do: Run west toward Westminster and Big Ben or east to the City and Blackfriars.
places.tip: A continuous, traffic-separated riverside path — one of central London’s best straight runs.

places.name: The Queen’s Walk (South Bank)
places.blurb: The buzzing South Bank riverside promenade facing the City skyline.
places.see: The London Eye, the Royal Festival Hall, skateboarders at the Undercroft, and St Paul’s across the river.
places.do: Follow it from Westminster Bridge past the Tate Modern toward Tower Bridge.
places.tip: Packed with strollers midday; run it early or push the pace at dawn.

places.name: Regent’s Canal Towpath
places.blurb: A quiet canalside towpath threading north London below street level.
places.see: Narrowboats and locks, the leafy edge of Regent’s Park, and the villas of Little Venice.
places.do: Run west to Little Venice or east toward Camden Lock and the markets.
places.tip: Narrow and shared with cyclists — keep left and mind the blind bridge holes.

places.name: Chelsea Embankment
places.blurb: A handsome Thames-side stretch past the gardens of Chelsea.
places.see: The red suspension cables of Albert Bridge, houseboats moored at Cheyne Walk, and plane trees along the river.
places.do: Connect to Battersea Park across the bridge or run on toward Pimlico.

places.name: Thames Path at Millennium Bridge
places.blurb: The City riverside walk beneath the dome of St Paul’s.
places.see: St Paul’s Cathedral above the north bank and the slender Millennium Bridge spanning to the Tate Modern.
places.do: Cross the Millennium Bridge to link the City with the South Bank.

places.name: The Mall
places.blurb: The ceremonial red avenue sweeping up to Buckingham Palace.
places.see: The Victoria Memorial and palace gates at one end, Admiralty Arch and Trafalgar Square at the other.
places.do: Run the processional route, then loop into St James’s Park alongside.
places.tip: Closed to traffic on Sundays — the smoothest ceremonial mile in the city.

places.name: The Serpentine, Hyde Park
places.blurb: The lake at the heart of Hyde Park, ringed by a popular running loop.
places.see: Rowing boats and swimmers on the water, the Diana Memorial fountain, and open parkland in every direction.
places.do: Circle the lake, then strike out across the park on Rotten Row or the Broad Walk.
places.tip: The full Serpentine loop is a classic ~2 mile circuit; join the dawn swimmers for a cold dip.

places.name: Rotten Row, Hyde Park
places.blurb: A broad sand horse-riding track running the length of Hyde Park.
places.see: Riders exercising their horses, the Albert Memorial’s gilded spire, and long avenues of trees.
places.do: A soft-surface alternative to the pavements; links Hyde Park Corner to Kensington.

places.name: Kensington Gardens Broad Walk
places.blurb: A wide tree-lined promenade through the calmer western half of the royal parks.
places.see: Kensington Palace, the Round Pond with its model boats, and the Italian Gardens fountains.
places.do: Run from the palace down to the Serpentine to join Hyde Park.

places.name: Regent’s Park Broad Walk
places.blurb: The grand central avenue of Regent’s Park, lined with formal gardens.
places.see: The Avenue Gardens’ fountains and urns, the dome of the central mosque, and the heights of Primrose Hill beyond.
places.do: Run the Broad Walk then take on the short, sharp climb of Primrose Hill for the skyline view.

places.name: Tower Bridge
places.blurb: The Victorian bascule bridge whose twin towers are a symbol of the city.
places.see: The blue-and-white drawbridge, the Tower of London on the bank, and the Pool of London opening downstream.
places.do: Cross the river here to link the South Bank with the City and St Katharine Docks.
places.tip: Check the bridge-lift times posted online — the road deck opens for tall ships.

places.name: Sky Garden
places.blurb: A free public garden under glass atop the “Walkie-Talkie” tower.
places.see: A 360° panorama over the Thames, the Shard, and the City from 35 floors up.
places.do: A destination viewpoint to bookend a City run — book the free timed entry ahead.
places.tip: Indoors and ticketed (free); a finish-line reward rather than a running stop.

places.name: The Garden at 120
places.blurb: A free rooftop garden terrace in the heart of the City.
places.see: Close-up views of the Gherkin, the Leadenhall “Cheesegrater,” and the cluster of City towers.
places.do: A quick lift up for a skyline breather on a City loop.

places.name: Victoria Embankment Gardens
places.blurb: A ribbon of riverside gardens tucked behind the Embankment.
places.see: Bandstand lawns, statues, and flowerbeds a step back from the Thames traffic.
places.do: A shaded, flat connector between Embankment and the river path.

places.name: Victoria Tower Gardens
places.blurb: A riverside park right beside the Houses of Parliament.
places.see: The Victoria Tower of Parliament, Rodin’s Burghers of Calais, and the river curving toward Lambeth Bridge.
places.do: A green pause directly under Westminster on a Thames-side run.

places.name: Russell Square
places.blurb: One of Bloomsbury’s largest and leafiest garden squares.
places.see: A central fountain, mature planes, and the terracotta façade of the Hotel Russell.
places.do: A calm lap in the museum quarter, steps from the British Museum.

places.name: Queen Square Gardens
places.blurb: A small, quiet Bloomsbury square among the hospitals and old houses.
places.see: Shaded benches, a statue of Queen Charlotte, and ivy-clad Georgian terraces.

places.name: Brunswick Square Gardens
places.blurb: A leafy Bloomsbury square beside the Foundling Museum.
places.see: One of London’s oldest plane trees and lawns shared with the neighbouring Coram’s Fields.

places.name: Lincoln’s Inn
places.blurb: The grounds of one of the four historic Inns of Court.
places.see: Tudor brick gatehouses, the chapel, and lawns backing onto Lincoln’s Inn Fields, London’s largest square.
places.do: Thread the quiet legal quarter between Holborn and the Royal Courts of Justice.
places.tip: The Inn’s private gates close in the evening; the adjoining Fields stay open.

places.name: Gray’s Inn Gardens
places.blurb: The serene private gardens (“The Walks”) of Gray’s Inn.
places.see: Long lawns and ancient plane trees said to have been planted by Francis Bacon.
places.tip: Open to the public only on weekday lunchtimes.

places.name: Middle Temple Garden
places.blurb: A riverside lawn within the medieval Temple, between Fleet Street and the Thames.
places.see: Tudor halls, the round Temple Church, and a garden tied in legend to the Wars of the Roses.
places.do: A hidden green detour off the Victoria Embankment.

places.name: Mount Street Gardens
places.blurb: A sheltered, sun-trap garden hidden in the heart of Mayfair.
places.see: London plane and Australian mimosa trees, songbirds, and rows of memorial benches.
places.do: A quiet breather amid Mayfair’s grand streets.

places.name: Phoenix Garden
places.blurb: A small community wildlife garden steps from the West End theatres.
places.see: Cottage planting, a pond, and the city’s only central-London frogs, behind Soho’s bustle.

places.name: Chelsea Physic Garden
places.blurb: London’s oldest botanic garden, walled beside the river in Chelsea.
places.see: Rare medicinal plants, glasshouses, and Britain’s largest outdoor fruiting olive tree.
places.do: A walled-garden landmark just off the Chelsea Embankment.
places.tip: Ticketed and gated — a passing landmark rather than a through-route.

places.name: Red Cross Garden
places.blurb: A restored Victorian “open-air sitting room” in Southwark.
places.see: A bandstand, pond, and cottage gardens laid out by social reformer Octavia Hill.
places.do: A green pause near Borough Market on a South Bank loop.

places.name: St Pancras Old Church & Gardens
places.blurb: A churchyard garden behind the stations, one of London’s oldest sites of worship.
places.see: The ancient church, Sir John Soane’s tomb, and the Hardy Tree ringed by gravestones.
places.do: A quiet detour from the Regent’s Canal towpath nearby.
places.transit: King’s Cross St Pancras (Northern, Victoria, Piccadilly)

places.name: Fortune Street Park
places.blurb: A neighbourhood green on the edge of the Barbican and the City.
places.see: Lawns and ball courts hemmed in by the Barbican’s concrete towers.
places.do: A handy turnaround on a City fringe run toward the Barbican.

places.name: Leicester Square
places.blurb: The West End’s film-premiere square, ringed by cinemas and crowds.
places.see: The Shakespeare fountain, movie-star handprints, and the bright lights of the theatre district.
places.do: A central crossroads between Soho, Covent Garden, and Trafalgar Square.
places.tip: Heaving with crowds day and night — pass through, don’t linger.

places.name: Allée des Cygnes
places.blurb: A slender tree-lined island in the middle of the Seine, made for running.
places.see: The Seine on both sides, the Pont de Bir-Hakeim overhead, and a quarter-scale Statue of Liberty at the downstream tip.
places.do: Run the full length of the islet and circle the little Liberty before doubling back.
places.tip: Car-free and flat; one of the most peaceful stretches of riverside in the city.

places.name: Tuileries Riverside Terrace
places.blurb: The raised Seine-side terrace running the length of the Jardin des Tuileries.
places.see: Gravel allées and clipped chestnuts on one side, the river and the Musée d’Orsay across the water on the other.
places.do: Link west to the Place de la Concorde or east under the Louvre arches.
places.tip: The garden gates close at night; run it by day for the full Louvre-to-Concorde sweep.

places.name: Quai Branly Riverside
places.blurb: Left-bank Seine promenade running straight beneath the Eiffel Tower.
places.see: The Tower rising directly above, bateaux-mouches on the river, and the gardens of the Quai Branly museum.
places.do: Continue to the Champ de Mars or cross the Pont de l’Alma to the Right Bank.
places.tip: Busy with tourists by midday near the Tower; go early for clear running.

places.name: Jardins du Trocadéro
places.blurb: Cascading fountains and lawns sloping down to the Seine opposite the Eiffel Tower.
places.see: The grand fountain basin, the Palais de Chaillot wings, and the postcard Tower view across the river.
places.do: Climb the steps to the Trocadéro esplanade for the classic photo line.

places.name: Coulée verte René-Dumont
places.blurb: An elevated planted greenway atop a former railway viaduct — the inspiration for New York’s High Line.
places.see: Rose arbours and grasses running above the 12th arrondissement, with rooftop-level views over Bastille.
places.do: Run it east toward the Bois de Vincennes or descend to the Viaduc des Arts arcades below.
places.tip: Narrow in places; ease off the pace where it threads between buildings.

places.name: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont Lake Loop
places.blurb: A dramatic hilly park built on old quarries, with a cliff-island temple in a lake.
places.see: The suspension footbridge, the Temple de la Sibylle on its crag, and waterfalls tumbling into the lake.
places.do: Loop the lake then take on the steep climbs the park is loved (and feared) for.
places.tip: The hills here are the real thing — a proper interval workout in the northeast of the city.

places.name: Jardin des Plantes
places.blurb: The city’s historic botanical garden, laid out in long formal allées.
places.see: Perspective rows of plane trees, the Natural History galleries, and a small menagerie zoo.
places.do: Run the central allée end to end, then loop out along the Seine quais nearby.

places.name: Place du Trocadéro
places.blurb: The great esplanade between the Palais de Chaillot wings — the best Eiffel Tower view in Paris.
places.see: The full Tower framed across the Seine, with the fountains stepping down toward the river below.
places.do: Pause for the view, then drop down through the gardens to the riverside.
places.tip: Arrive at sunrise for the Tower light and empty pavements.

places.name: Montmartre & Sacré-Cœur
places.blurb: The hilltop village crowned by the white domes of the Sacré-Cœur basilica.
places.see: All of Paris spread below from the basilica steps, plus the artists’ square of Place du Tertre behind.
places.do: Grind up the stairways and lanes, then wind down the quiet north side of the butte.
places.tip: It’s the highest point in the city — expect a real climb and crowded steps up top.

places.name: Arc de Triomphe
places.blurb: Napoleon’s triumphal arch at the hub of twelve radiating avenues.
places.see: The Champs-Élysées sweeping down toward the Louvre and, the other way, La Défense on the horizon.
places.do: Circle the Étoile via the pedestrian underpass, never the traffic ring.
places.tip: Use the underpass to reach the arch — the roundabout is one of the busiest in Europe.

places.name: Notre-Dame & Île de la Cité
places.blurb: The Gothic cathedral at the very heart of Paris, on the island where the city began.
places.see: The restored spire and flying buttresses, the Seine wrapping the island, and the booksellers’ green boxes along the quais.
places.do: Loop the island on the riverside quais for cathedral views from every angle.

places.name: Pont des Arts
places.blurb: The wooden pedestrian bridge linking the Louvre to the Institut de France.
places.see: A clean sightline down the Seine to the Île de la Cité, with the Louvre on one bank and the Académie dome on the other.
places.do: Cross between the Right and Left Banks here on a riverside loop.

places.name: Square du Vert-Galant
places.blurb: A leafy little park at the downstream prow of the Île de la Cité, right at water level.
places.see: The Seine splitting around the island’s point and the arches of the Pont Neuf overhead.
places.do: Drop down the steps from the Pont Neuf for a quiet riverside breather.
places.tip: Floods after heavy rain; closed when the river runs high.

places.name: Jardin du Palais-Royal
