places.blurb: A serene arcaded garden hidden behind the former royal palace.
places.see: Symmetrical lime-tree avenues, fountains, and Buren’s striped columns in the forecourt.
places.do: A calm, flat lap moments from the Louvre — good for an easy warm-up.

places.name: Louvre & Jardin du Carrousel
places.blurb: The palace courtyards and gardens linking the Louvre to the Tuileries.
places.see: I. M. Pei’s glass pyramid, the pink Arc du Carrousel, and the grand axis stretching to the Concorde obelisk.
places.do: Run the historic axis from the pyramid out through the Tuileries.

places.name: Palais Garnier (Opéra)
places.blurb: The opulent 19th-century opera house that gave the Phantom its setting.
places.see: A gilded, statue-crowned façade closing the view up the Avenue de l’Opéra.
places.do: Use it as a turnaround on a Right Bank loop through the grands boulevards.

places.name: Conciergerie
places.blurb: A medieval royal palace turned Revolutionary prison on the Île de la Cité.
places.see: Round defensive towers along the Seine and the city’s oldest public clock on the corner.
places.do: Pass it on a riverside loop of the island toward Notre-Dame.

places.name: Square de la Tour Saint-Jacques
places.blurb: A small garden around a lone flamboyant-Gothic tower near Châtelet.
places.see: The lacy stone tower — all that remains of a vanished church — rising over the flowerbeds.

places.name: Square Marie-Trintignant
places.blurb: A riverside garden on the Right Bank quays at the edge of the Marais.
places.see: The Seine and the tip of the Île Saint-Louis just across the water.
places.do: Connect along the quais toward the Île Saint-Louis bridges.

places.name: Jardin Nelson-Mandela (Les Halles)
places.blurb: The big central garden above the Forum des Halles, on the old market site.
places.see: Open lawns and play areas under the rippling glass Canopée roof, with Saint-Eustache church alongside.
places.do: A flat green crossroads linking the Louvre, the Marais, and the river.

places.name: Jardin de Kyiv
places.blurb: A quiet terraced garden behind the Place de la Concorde gardens.
places.see: Hedged walks a short hop from the Tuileries and the Madeleine.

places.name: Musée des Arts et Métiers
places.blurb: A science-and-industry museum in a former priory at the edge of the Marais.
places.see: Foucault’s pendulum and early flying machines inside; a steampunk-tiled métro station below.
places.do: A landmark turn on a northern Marais loop.

places.name: Bastille
places.blurb: The lively square where the Revolution began, now a hub of cafés and nightlife.
places.see: The bronze July Column with its gilded spirit of Liberty at the centre of the roundabout.
places.do: Start the Coulée verte greenway here, or head to the Marais and the river.

places.name: Promenade d’Australie
places.blurb: A right-bank riverside walk below the Passy hill, opposite the Allée des Cygnes.
places.see: The Seine, the Pont de Bir-Hakeim’s iron deck, and the Eiffel Tower downstream.
places.do: Drop onto the Allée des Cygnes island midstream from the bridge.

places.name: Square Jean-XXIII
places.blurb: The garden directly behind Notre-Dame, along the tip of the Île de la Cité.
places.see: The cathedral’s east end and flying buttresses rising straight above the rose beds.
places.do: Best vantage on Notre-Dame’s spire; pair it with an island riverside loop.

places.name: Hôtel de Ville
places.blurb: The grand neo-Renaissance city hall facing a wide riverside plaza.
places.see: An ornate statue-lined façade and the open square that turns into an ice rink each winter.
places.do: A natural Right Bank waypoint between the Marais and the Île de la Cité.

places.name: Musée de la Légion d’Honneur
places.blurb: An elegant mansion museum on the Left Bank beside the Musée d’Orsay.
places.see: The Hôtel de Salm’s rotunda and, next door, Orsay’s great clock-faced railway hall.
places.do: Cut to the Seine here and pick up the Left Bank quais.

places.name: Clos Montmartre & Jardin Saint-Vincent
places.blurb: Paris’s last working vineyard, tucked into the quiet north slope of Montmartre.
places.see: Terraced vines, the pink Au Lapin Agile cabaret, and steep village lanes with no crowds.
places.do: Loop the calm back side of the butte away from the Sacré-Cœur tourist crush.

places.name: Sumida River Terrace
places.blurb: Continuous riverside promenade tracing the Sumida toward Asakusa and Tokyo Skytree.
places.see: The river opens wide between historic bridges, with Tokyo Skytree spiking above the far bank.
places.do: Run the full terrace up to Azuma Bridge and the Asakusa waterfront.
places.tip: Best at dusk when the bridges and Skytree light up; pavement floods only in extreme high water.

places.name: Meguro River (Naka-Meguro)
places.blurb: The willow-and-cherry canal that turns Naka-Meguro into Tokyo's most photographed blossom corridor.
places.see: Cherry branches arch over the narrow river, reflected in the water beside canalside cafes.
places.do: Trace the canal between the low bridges of Naka-Meguro.
places.tip: Late March to early April for sakura; go early morning to beat the crowds.

places.name: Odaiba South Route
places.blurb: Bayfront path along Odaiba with open views across Tokyo Bay.
places.see: The Rainbow Bridge and the bay's wide horizon stretch out beyond the seawall.
places.do: Run the waterfront toward Odaiba Seaside Park and the bay overlooks.
places.tip: Exposed and breezy; sunset over the bridge is the payoff.

places.name: Chidorigafuchi Greenway
places.blurb: Cherry-lined greenway along the Imperial Palace's northwest moat.
places.see: Old cherry trees lean over the green moat water with the palace woods behind.
places.do: Follow the greenway above the moat toward Kudanshita.
places.tip: Iconic in sakura season; rowboats fill the moat below on weekends.

places.name: Seaside Terrace
places.blurb: Quiet canal-side terrace near the Shibaura waterfront.
places.see: Still canal water mirrors the surrounding towers and footbridges.
places.do: Loop the green terrace along the water's edge.
places.tip: Calm and uncrowded; pleasant on a warm evening.

places.name: Green Walk
places.blurb: Short leafy waterside path near Hamarikyu and the Shiodome canals.
places.see: Greenery frames the canal with Shiodome's glass towers rising beyond.
places.do: Link it into a Hamarikyu Gardens loop.
places.tip: Best paired with the gardens rather than run on its own.

places.name: Imperial Palace Plaza
places.blurb: The moat-side plaza at the heart of Tokyo's famous Imperial Palace running loop.
places.see: Manicured pines and the stone-walled moat front the palace's Nijubashi bridges.
places.do: Join the 5km Imperial Palace loop, Tokyo's classic runners' circuit.
places.tip: Run counter-clockwise like the locals; busiest at weekday dawn and dusk.

places.name: Meiji Shrine South Approach
places.blurb: Forested gravel approach leading through Meiji Shrine's torii gates.
places.see: Towering cypress and a giant wooden torii enclose the path in deep green calm.
places.do: Walk the sando up to the shrine's main hall in the heart of the forest.
places.tip: A reverent space; walk rather than run on the shrine grounds proper.

places.name: Kitajikken River Waterside Terrace
places.blurb: Waterside terrace beneath Tokyo Skytree along the Kitajikken River.
places.see: Skytree towers straight overhead, mirrored in the canal at your feet.
places.do: Run the terrace to the Sumida confluence near Asakusa.
places.tip: Unbeatable Skytree photos from the water's edge after dark.

places.name: Yoyogi Park Cycling Course
places.localName: 代々木公園サイクリングコース
places.blurb: Wide tree-shaded loop through Yoyogi Park, a runners' and cyclists' favorite.
places.see: Broad lawns and tall zelkova give way to fountains and open sky.
places.do: Circle the park loop, then branch onto the cycling course.
places.tip: Lively on weekends with buskers and dancers near Harajuku gate.

places.name: Times Avenue
places.blurb: Landscaped pedestrian avenue threading the West Shinjuku skyscraper district.
places.see: Glass-and-steel towers rise on every side above a tidy planted walkway.
places.do: Connect it toward the Tokyo Metropolitan Government towers.
places.tip: Sheltered and quiet on weekends when the offices empty out.

places.name: Shinjuku Southern Terrace
places.blurb: Tree-lined deck promenade running south from Shinjuku Station.
places.see: Seasonal illuminations and planters line the raised walk above the tracks.
places.do: Stroll the terrace toward Yoyogi past cafes and shops.
places.tip: Famous winter light displays from November through February.

places.name: Takeshita Street
places.blurb: Harajuku's narrow, neon-bright youth-fashion shopping street.
places.see: Crepe stands, costume shops and crowds spill along the packed lane.
places.do: Window-shop the length of the street to Meiji-dori.
places.tip: Shoulder-to-shoulder on weekends; come early morning to actually move.

places.name: Ebisu Skywalk
places.localName: 恵比寿スカイウォーク
places.blurb: Covered moving-walkway corridor linking Ebisu Station to Yebisu Garden Place.
places.see: A long glass gallery leads to the Garden Place plaza and its chateau facade.
places.do: Glide the skywalk out to the Garden Place gardens.
places.tip: A handy all-weather connector rather than a run in itself.

places.name: Tamagawa Aqueduct Promenade
places.localName: 玉川上水・内藤新宿分水散歩道
places.blurb: Green historic-aqueduct walk along the old Naito Shinjuku branch channel.
places.see: A slim ribbon of trees and restored watercourse threads between buildings.
places.do: Follow the promenade toward Shinjuku Gyoen's west edge.
places.tip: A leafy shortcut linking Shinjuku to the garden gates.

places.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Observation Deck
places.blurb: Free 202m observation decks atop the twin-towered Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building.
places.see: A free-of-charge panorama sweeps from the Shinjuku skyline to Mt. Fuji on clear days.
places.do: Ride up to the north or south observatory before or after a Shinjuku run.
places.tip: Free entry; clearest Fuji views on crisp winter mornings.

places.name: Shibuya Crossing Viewpoint
places.localName: 渋谷スクランブル交差点
places.blurb: The pedestrian-bridge view over the world's busiest scramble crossing.
places.see: Waves of people surge across the intersection beneath towering video screens.
places.do: Watch from the station footbridge, then cross with the throng.
places.tip: Most dramatic after dark when the screens blaze; rush hour for peak crowds.

places.name: Tokyo City View (Roppongi)
places.blurb: Sky-high observation deck atop Roppongi Hills Mori Tower.
places.see: A 360-degree sweep takes in Tokyo Tower glowing red against the city grid.
places.do: Ride up for the indoor deck and, in season, the open-air Sky Deck.
places.tip: Sunset to blue hour is best; the rooftop Sky Deck is weather-dependent.

places.name: Okura Garden
places.blurb: Pocket Japanese garden beside the Hotel Okura near the Imperial grounds.
places.see: A small pond, stone lanterns and clipped pines make a quiet city refuge.
places.do: Pause here between Toranomon and the palace moat.
places.tip: A calm breather just steps from Okura Museum of Art.

places.name: Kabukicho
places.blurb: Shinjuku's electric entertainment and nightlife district.
places.see: Walls of neon and giant screens, anchored by the Godzilla head over Toho Cinemas.
places.do: Cut through the lantern-lit lanes toward Golden Gai.
places.tip: Comes alive after dark; busy and best explored on foot.

places.name: Hibiya Godzilla Square
places.localName: 日比谷ゴジラスクエア
places.blurb: Plaza marked by a life-sized Godzilla statue beside Hibiya's theaters.
places.see: The bronze Godzilla rears up amid the greenery near Hibiya Park.
places.do: Snap the statue en route between Ginza and the palace moat.
places.tip: A quick, fun landmark on the way into Hibiya Park.

places.name: Midtown Garden
places.localName: ミッドタウンガーデン
places.blurb: Spacious lawns and tree groves behind Tokyo Midtown in Roppongi.
places.see: Broad grass and a curving tree-lined path open out behind the towers.
places.do: Run the garden loop and link into adjacent Hinokicho Park.
places.tip: Cherry trees here are a quieter sakura spot than the big parks.

places.name: Hotel New Otani Japanese Garden
places.localName: ホテルニューオータニ日本庭園
places.blurb: A 400-year-old strolling garden tucked behind the Hotel New Otani.
places.see: A red bridge, koi pond and a tumbling waterfall sit hidden among old trees.
places.do: Wander the garden path between Akasaka and the palace.
places.tip: Open to the public and free; lovely in autumn color.

places.name: Tokyu Plaza Omotesando Harajuku Rooftop
places.localName: 東急プラザ表参道原宿
places.blurb: Leafy rooftop terrace above the mirror-clad mall at Omotesando's corner.
places.see: A small wood deck and greenery overlook the Harajuku–Omotesando crossing.
places.do: Take the kaleidoscope escalators up for a rooftop breather.
places.tip: Free rooftop with a cafe; good views down Omotesando.

places.name: Ueno Station & Ameyoko Viewpoint
places.blurb: Overlook of the rail fan-out at Ueno beside the Ameyoko market lanes.
places.see: Trains splay across the throat of Ueno Station above the bustling Ameyoko stalls.
places.do: Watch the trains, then dive into the Ameyoko market.
places.tip: Market is liveliest late afternoon; chaotic and fun before New Year.

places.name: Shiodome Sio-Site
places.blurb: Skyscraper complex of plazas and skywalks beside Hamarikyu Gardens.
places.see: Glass towers and elevated decks frame views toward the bay and gardens.
places.do: Cross the skywalks linking Shimbashi to the Hamarikyu waterfront.
places.tip: A good staging point for a Hamarikyu Gardens loop.

places.name: Marunouchi House
places.blurb: Open-air dining terrace overlooking the Marunouchi business district.
places.see: City lights and office towers spread out from the breezy 7th-floor deck.
places.do: Pause for a drink with a view between Tokyo Station and Ginza.
places.tip: Terrace tables are best on warm evenings after work hours.

places.name: Akihabara Park
places.blurb: Small green plaza beside the electronics-town bustle of Akihabara.
places.see: A patch of trees and benches offers a pause amid the neon and arcades.
places.do: Rest here between Akihabara's gadget shops and the Kanda River.
places.tip: A handy breather in an otherwise concrete district.

places.name: Kiyosumi 2-chome Park
places.blurb: Neighborhood park in the old-Tokyo district near Kiyosumi Gardens.
places.see: Shaded benches and play areas sit among the low streets of Fukagawa.
places.do: Use it as a turnaround near the Sumida and Kiyosumi Gardens.
places.tip: Pairs well with a visit to nearby Kiyosumi Teien.

places.name: Ueno Park & Shinobazu Pond
places.blurb: Tokyo's grand museum park, ringed by cherry trees above a lotus-filled pond.
places.see: Cherry avenues and temple roofs surround Shinobazu Pond's summer carpet of lotus.
places.do: Loop the pond and run the cherry-lined museum promenades.
places.tip: Peak sakura crowds in early April; lotus blooms in midsummer.

places.name: Baseball Hall of Fame Museum
places.blurb: Japan's baseball museum beside Tokyo Dome.
places.see: Bats, jerseys and the hall of plaques sit under the Tokyo Dome's white roof.
places.do: Detour in while looping the Koishikawa and Tokyo Dome area.
places.tip: Easy add-on to a run past the dome's amusement park.

places.name: Sky Circus Sunshine 60 Observatory
places.localName: サンシャイン60展望台 スカイサーカス
places.blurb: High-tech 251m observation deck atop Ikebukuro's Sunshine 60 tower.
places.see: Mirror-walled galleries and VR rides frame a north-side panorama of the city.
places.do: Ride up after exploring Ikebukuro's east side.
places.tip: Ticketed; the interactive exhibits make it kid-friendly.

places.name: Seiko Museum Ginza
places.localName: セイコーミュージアム
places.blurb: Watchmaking museum in the heart of Ginza near the famous Wako clock tower.
places.see: Antique timepieces and the story of Japanese horology fill the Ginza gallery.
places.do: Pair it with a stroll down Ginza's flagship-lined Chuo-dori.
places.tip: Reserve ahead; Ginza is at its grandest on car-free weekend afternoons.

places.name: Bank of Japan Currency Museum
places.localName: 日本銀行金融研究所貨幣博物館
places.blurb: Free museum of Japanese money beside the historic Bank of Japan in Nihonbashi.
places.see: Centuries of coins, gold oban and old banknotes line the quiet exhibition halls.
places.do: Detour in while running the Nihonbashi river and bridge district.
places.tip: Free entry; closed Mondays.

places.name: Pumpkin (Yayoi Kusama)
places.blurb: Yayoi Kusama's polka-dotted pumpkin sculpture in the Marunouchi district.
places.see: The artist's signature bright, dotted gourd pops against the office towers.
places.do: Snap the sculpture between Tokyo Station and the Imperial Palace.
places.tip: A quick, photogenic stop on the Marunouchi side of the station.

places.name: Flower Plaza
places.blurb: Small planted plaza near the Marunouchi and Yaesu waterfront edge.
places.see: Seasonal flower beds brighten a paved square among the office blocks.
places.do: Pause here on a loop between Tokyo Station and the river.
places.tip: A pleasant green breather in a dense business quarter.
